task.description: WF-03 Step 3 for ISS-0427: implement the gate-approved design (lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md) -- Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate (test/support/tenant_template.ex), its 13-dimension assert_clone_parity!/2, and wiring TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 to use it with the design's explicit opt-out. Verify with real output: compile, format, a real parity-check pass against a real clone, a deliberately broken clone proving the check is non-vacuous, a before/after timing measurement, and a real test-file run.

result.summary:
IMPLEMENTED per the design, then found a REAL, CONFIRMED FALSE PREMISE in the design during end-to-end verification -- stopping and reporting rather than improvising past it, per this run's own explicit instruction and per two prior gates already having caught false premises on this run.

WHAT WAS BUILT (compiles clean, formatted clean, both verified with real command output below):

1. test/support/tenant_template.ex -- new module Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate. ensure_template!/0 (session-level pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock, not the transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock the design's §4.3 text suggested -- see DEVIATION below), template_ready?/0, template_schema_name/0, clone_tenant_schema!/1 (design §2.3 steps 1-8: CREATE SCHEMA, per-table CREATE TABLE LIKE INCLUDING ALL, FK re-add with schema-qualifier rewrite (§0.1 finding 1), sequence recreation + default repoint + OWNED BY (§0.1 findings 3-4), event_type_registry data copy, schema_migrations clone+copy, Registration row insert), and assert_clone_parity!/2 implementing all 13 comparison dimensions from design §3.2.
2. test/support/tenant_fixture.ex -- provisioned_tenant!/1 gained opts[:template] (:clone default / :replay escape hatch, design §4.1/INV-2), branching to Letflow.Test.TenantTemplate.ensure_template!/0 + clone_tenant_schema!/1 or the original provision_tenant_schema/1 + replay_migrations/1 sequence unchanged. assert_schema_complete!/2 (step 6) runs unconditionally on either path, unchanged.

ZERO lib/ diff -- confirmed via git status --porcelain: only test/support/tenant_template.ex (new) and test/support/tenant_fixture.ex (modified) touched. Zero change to TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 or replay_migrations/2's own bodies -- design §7's production-path-untouched claim holds exactly as specified; OQ-1 was resolved as option (b) (design §2.2/§9 OQ-1): the template is built by inserting a throwaway real Tenant + a throwaway Registration row (via Repo.insert_all/3, bypassing Registration.changeset/2's validate_format/3 deliberately and explained inline -- that validation exists specifically to reject 'tenant_template' as INV-1 requires, so this transient row is the one sanctioned exception, and both throwaway rows are deleted before build_template!/0 returns, keeping the schema itself), then calling the REAL, unmodified replay_migrations/2 against it -- so the production event-type-seeding logic runs unmodified and no new public function was added to lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE DESIGN'S LITERAL TEXT, both load-bearing, both found by actually running the mechanism against Postgres rather than reasoning about it, recorded per core-directives.md 'Never resolve a conflict silently':

DEVIATION 1 (mechanism-breaking if followed literally). Design §4.3 says ensure_template!/0's build sequence should be wrapped in 'the SAME pg_advisory_xact_lock pattern provision_tenant_schema/1 already uses' inside one Repo.transaction. Implemented literally first -- it failed hard: replay_migrations/2's own Ecto.Migrator.run/4 checks out its OWN connection rather than participating in the ambient Repo.transaction's connection/transaction, so the CREATE SCHEMA issued inside that outer transaction was invisible to the migrator ("schema \"tenant_template\" does not exist", Postgrex error code 3F000, reproduced and quoted in full during this step's own verification). Fixed by using a SESSION-level pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock pair (explicit unlock in an after block so a raise still releases it) instead of the transaction-scoped lock, and NOT wrapping build_template!/0 in a Repo.transaction at all -- matching SandboxPool.provision_sandbox/2's own established pattern of plain sequential Repo.query!/Ecto.Migrator.run calls with no wrapping transaction. clone_tenant_schema!/1 (which never calls replay_migrations/2, only raw Repo.query! DDL) is still wrapped in one Repo.transaction, matching design §2.3 as written -- this deviation is scoped to ensure_template!/0 only.

DEVIATION 2 (test bug in this implementation, not a design defect -- fixed here). Dimension #2's comparison of raw information_schema.columns.ordinal_position false-failed on every table with a dropped column (e.g. instance_projections, users -- REQ-064's tenant_id-drop migrations leave a permanent ordinal gap in the TEMPLATE that LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL does not preserve in the clone, which renumbers to consecutive positions). Fixed by re-ranking each side's own column list to a relative 1..N index before comparing, so RELATIVE order is asserted (what the design's dimension #2 actually needs) rather than the raw absolute integer (which LIKE was never claimed to preserve). Same root cause also silently corrected an equivalent risk in dimension #4 (indexes): the auto-renamed index identifiers design §0.1 finding 2 documents were being compared as part of the full indexdef STRING including the name, which is exactly the name-based comparison the design explicitly says dimension #4 must NOT do -- my first implementation did it anyway (bug, not a design gap) and it produced real false-fail noise (105/105 indexes, all reported as mismatched, on a structurally-correct clone) until fixed to strip the index's own name and compare only the ON-clause-forward structural remainder, uniqueness tracked separately. Same name-stripping technique applied preemptively to dimension #11 (pg_statistic_ext) for the same reason design §0.2 finding 4 documents, though that dimension is currently a zero-vs-zero rule-out in this codebase (verified, see below) so it was not exercised by this session's real data.

=== THE BLOCKING FINDING: design's trigger dormancy claim is FALSE, confirmed against the real database, not reasoned about ===

Design §3.2 item 8 (and §0.2 finding 7's REWORK NOTE, and §11's acceptance-criteria table) states: 'no migration under priv/repo/migrations/ contains CREATE TRIGGER or CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER in any execute/1 call' -- grepped, claimed zero hits, repeated across THREE separate design passes (original, rework 1, rework 2) and independently re-verified by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at both re-gates. On that basis, dimension #8 is specified as a bare count-equal-to-zero assertion, and no mechanism step exists in §2.3 to recreate triggers in a clone (this gap is explicitly named as OQ-2, 'not designed here since no trigger exists today').

This claim is FALSE. Re-grepped myself, independently, before relying on it: `grep -rln "CREATE TRIGGER" priv/repo/migrations/*.exs` returns TWO files -- priv/repo/migrations/20260830020001_create_audit_entries_tenant_scoped.exs (CREATE TRIGGER audit_entries_no_update, audit_entries_no_delete) and priv/repo/migrations/20260830030001_create_repository_artifacts.exs (CREATE TRIGGER repository_artifacts_no_update, repository_artifacts_no_delete, artifact_versions_no_update) -- five real triggers total, each backed by a real CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION (audit_entries_immutable/0, repository_artifacts_immutable/0, artifact_versions_immutable/0), each enforcing real immutability semantics (RAISE EXCEPTION on UPDATE/DELETE against audit_entries, repository_artifacts, artifact_versions). CONFIRMED AGAINST A REAL, FRESHLY-BUILT TEMPLATE, not just the migration source: `SELECT count(*) FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid=t.tgrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='tenant_template' AND NOT t.tgisinternal` returned 5 on a template this step itself built via the real, unmodified replay_migrations/2 (i.e. these are genuinely reachable via the production migration path, not a probe artifact). `\d tenant_template.audit_entries` independently confirmed the two audit_entries triggers by name and definition.

These two migrations are dated 20260830 -- after whatever point the design's repeated grep should have caught them, across three separate passes by two different roles (CODE-DESIGNER, CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR) on 2026-09-04. I am not asserting why the grep missed them (a stale grep target, a typo in the pattern, or the migrations landing on main between the design's passes and this implementation step are all possible and I did not investigate which) -- only that the CURRENT, real state of priv/repo/migrations/ contradicts the design's stated and re-verified premise, checked directly against Postgres, not inherited from the design's own claim.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DESIGN, stated precisely: dimension #8 as specified (assert trigger count equal to ZERO on both sides) is simply wrong against today's real schema -- the reference (template, migration-built) has 5, my mechanism's clone correctly has 0 (LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL is a documented exception for triggers, verified directly by this design's own §0.2/§0.3 probes and reconfirmed by my own clone's real behavior), so a literal implementation of dimension #8 either (a) as specified, asserting equal-to-zero, would silently PASS a clone that is actually missing five real, behaviorally load-bearing immutability triggers -- exactly the 'silently degraded schema' class of hazard this entire design exists to catch, now demonstrated live rather than hypothetical -- or (b) if I instead assert equal-COUNT (reference vs candidate, not equal-to-zero), the check correctly FAILS every real clone, because OQ-2's mechanism step ('not designed here') does not exist to make it pass. Neither option is something I can resolve myself: (a) satisfies the check by weakening what it measures, forbidden per core-directives.md's 'Never Satisfy a Gate by Editing What It Measures'; (b) requires designing and implementing a real trigger-recreation mechanism (create the two/three trigger functions and five triggers in the clone's own schema, repointed at the clone rather than the template) that the approved design explicitly states is out of scope and 'not designed here' -- CODE-DESIGNER's job, not mine, and REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER have not seen a trigger-recreation mechanism design to gate.

WHAT I DID INSTEAD OF GUESSING: implemented dimension #8 as equal-COUNT (option b above, the honest, non-vacuous version -- see 'What was built' above, check_triggers_comments/2 compares trigger_count(reference) to trigger_count(candidate), not either side to a literal 0), so the module I am handing off does NOT silently pass a degraded clone. This means: the parity check FAILS on every clone today, correctly and non-vacuously, because the clone mechanism genuinely does not yet recreate these five triggers. I did not implement a trigger-recreation mechanism to make it pass, because that is new design surface the approved design explicitly deferred (OQ-2) and did not specify -- inventing one myself would be exactly the 'design from scratch' this role is not authorized to do outside the §10 sizing-rule checklist, and this change (new DDL-generation logic touching a tenant-data schema shape, plus a correctness-critical immutability guarantee) does not plausibly pass that checklist.

=== VERIFICATION PERFORMED, WITH REAL OUTPUT (everything that COULD be verified before hitting the blocker) ===

1. MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors -- exit 0, clean, both test/support/tenant_template.ex and test/support/tenant_fixture.ex, run repeatedly across every fix in this step.
2. mix format --check-formatted (both files) -- exit 0, clean, no reformatting needed.
3. Real parity check run against a real clone (all 13 dimensions): confirmed WORKING CORRECTLY for every dimension except #8 -- dimensions #1 (table set), #2 (columns, after the ordinal-position fix), #3 (constraints), #4 (indexes, after the name-stripping fix), #5 (sequences, including the sequence-trap direction check), #6 (identity), #7 (row counts), #9 (reloptions, zero-vs-zero today, confirmed), #10 (attstattarget, zero-vs-zero today, confirmed), #11 (pg_statistic_ext, zero-vs-zero today, confirmed), #12 (ruled-out properties), #13 (type/collation namespace, pg_catalog-only today, confirmed) all correctly report zero diffs on a real, freshly-built clone. Only #8 (triggers) fails, and it fails CORRECTLY given the real database state -- this is the check doing its job, not a bug in the check.
4. NON-VACUOUS PROOF, both required scenarios run for real, against real data, before the trigger finding fully surfaced: (a) dropped a real FK constraint (group_members_group_id_fkey) from a real clone via ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT, then called assert_clone_parity!/2 -- it raised ExUnit.AssertionError citing the exact missing constraint under dimension #3, confirmed. (b) repointed a real sequence-backed column default (events.global_seq) at the TEMPLATE's own sequence via ALTER TABLE ... SET DEFAULT nextval(<template-qualified name>) -- reproducing the exact 'sequence trap' hazard ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis found -- then called assert_clone_parity!/2 -- it raised citing the exact namespace leak under dimension #5, confirmed. Both proofs demonstrate the check is genuinely non-vacuous for every dimension it currently asserts correctly.
5. TIMING: measured, but NOT representative of the design's ~2.5x claim, and I am not reporting a clean number as final because the mechanism as currently implemented is not yet complete (it lacks trigger recreation, so its measured cost is not the cost of a CORRECT clone). For honesty: 5-run averages on this host, this session, were clone ~845-880ms vs replay ~876-923ms -- roughly a 1.0x-1.05x ratio, NOT the ~2.5x the design's §10 states as its own honestly-hedged expectation. This is materially below expectation and I flag it plainly rather than massaging it, though I do not yet know how much of the gap is (i) the per-table-per-column N+1 query pattern my recreate_sequences!/1 uses (one pg_get_serial_sequence round trip per table x column pair across all 39 tables, dominated by this host's Docker Desktop round-trip tax per ISS-0432's own finding, the same tax that dominates both sides of this ratio) vs (ii) something else. This needs re-measurement once the trigger gap is closed and the mechanism is representative of what will actually ship -- reporting today's number as informational only, not as the final verified figure the task asked for, because the mechanism is not yet complete.
6. Real test-file run: NOT performed. No permanent test file exists yet for this module (test/support/tenant_template_test.exs is TEST-DESIGNER's artefact per design §3.4 item 2 -- explicitly not built in this step) and running the 49 existing provisioned_tenant!/1 call sites against the new :clone default would exercise a mechanism I already know produces a real, correct assertion failure (dimension #8) on every single one of them -- that would not be a meaningful verification run, it would just reproduce the same finding 49 times. Deferred until the blocker below is resolved.

All probe/scratch artifacts cleaned up before this handoff: scratch/probe_clone.exs, scratch/probe_diff.exs, and their output captures were deleted (scratch/ is git-ignored, confirmed via git status --porcelain showing zero untracked files there). Every probe schema (tenant_template and every cloned tenant_<hex> schema created during verification) was dropped via DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE, clones before template per this run's own instruction -- confirmed via `SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'tenant_%'` returning 0 rows. Every throwaway tenants/tenant_schemas row created during verification (including two left over from an earlier failed attempt, before the transaction-boundary deviation was fixed) was deleted -- confirmed via a slug LIKE query returning 0 rows. git status --porcelain shows exactly the two intended source files (test/support/tenant_template.ex new, test/support/tenant_fixture.ex modified) plus this handoff file -- nothing else.

issues.title: Design's trigger-dormancy premise (§3.2 item 8, §0.2 finding 7, §11) is factually false against the current priv/repo/migrations/ -- 5 real, behaviorally load-bearing immutability triggers exist (audit_entries x2, repository_artifacts x2, artifact_versions x1, from 20260830020001 and 20260830030001), confirmed directly against a real, freshly-built template schema, not inherited from the design's own repeated (and repeatedly wrong) grep claim.
issues.description: Design §3.2 dimension #8 specifies trigger count equal-to-ZERO on both sides, on the stated basis that no migration creates one -- restated and re-verified across three design passes and two CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gates, all reaching the same wrong conclusion. Re-grepping priv/repo/migrations/*.exs myself during this step's own verification found CREATE TRIGGER in two migration files dated 20260830, both real and both currently shipping in every tenant schema this codebase provisions today (production and test alike). This is not a hypothetical OQ-2 scenario ('if a future migration adds one') -- it is today's actual, current schema. A literal implementation of dimension #8 as specified would silently PASS a clone missing five real immutability triggers, which is exactly the class of silent-corruption hazard ISS-0427 and this entire design exist to prevent -- so I implemented the check as equal-COUNT instead (non-vacuous, correctly fails today), rather than satisfying the gate by implementing what the design literally says. The clone mechanism (§2.3) has no step to recreate triggers -- that is real, unbuilt design surface (symmetric in shape to the FK re-add and sequence-recreation steps already in §2.3), and building it myself would be designing from scratch outside this role's authorization for a change of this shape (new DDL-generation logic on a tenant-data schema path, correctness-critical). Needs to go back to CODE-DESIGNER: (1) correct the dormancy claim project-wide (§0.2 finding 7's REWORK NOTE and §3.2 item 8 both need updating, not just the trigger COUNT check), (2) design the actual trigger-recreation mechanism resolving OQ-2 for real (function body copy via pg_get_functiondef, schema-qualifier rewrite matching the FK-rewrite technique already proven in §0.1 finding 1, then CREATE TRIGGER in the clone's own schema), (3) re-verify no OTHER 'currently dormant, will catch it later' claim in this design has gone stale the same way in the 5 days since 20260830's migrations landed -- I did not have time/scope to re-audit every other dormancy claim (reloptions, attstattarget, pg_statistic_ext, custom types/collations, index/constraint comments) against today's migration tree beyond spot-confirming they are still zero-hit via grep during this step's own verification (all four re-confirmed zero-hit today, quoted in the summary above), so those four are NOT flagged as stale, only the trigger claim, which is the one I found actually contradicted by real data.

issues.title: Design §4.3's literal transaction-scoped pg_advisory_xact_lock wrapping for ensure_template!/0 does not work as written -- Ecto.Migrator.run/4 (inside replay_migrations/2, called by this step's OQ-1-option-(b) template build) checks out its own connection, so DDL issued inside an outer Repo.transaction is invisible to it. Fixed by using a session-level pg_advisory_lock/pg_advisory_unlock pair instead, not wrapped in a Repo.transaction, matching SandboxPool.provision_sandbox/2's own established sequential (non-transactional) pattern.
issues.description: Reproduced directly: literal implementation raised Postgrex error code 3F000 ('schema "tenant_template" does not exist') the first time ensure_template!/0 tried to build the template, because CREATE SCHEMA (issued inside the outer Repo.transaction) was never visible to Ecto.Migrator.run/4's own, separately-checked-out connection. This is a correction to the design's §4.3 text for future readers/CODE-DESIGNER, not something I resolved silently -- clone_tenant_schema!/1 (which never calls replay_migrations/2) is unaffected and still uses one Repo.transaction exactly as §2.3 specifies.

issues.title: Design's §2.3 step 7 (schema_migrations row copy) implicitly assumes the clone's own schema_migrations table already exists, but nothing in §2.3 steps 1-6 creates it (expected_tenant_tables/0 deliberately excludes schema_migrations, so the per-table LIKE loop never touches it) -- fixed by adding an explicit CREATE TABLE (LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL) for schema_migrations immediately before the row-copy INSERT.
issues.description: Reproduced directly: the literal step-7 INSERT ... SELECT raised Postgrex undefined_table (42P01) against the clone's nonexistent schema_migrations relation on the very first real clone attempt. Purely mechanical fix, not a design-intent change -- schema_migrations is the migrator's own bookkeeping table and cloning its structure via the same LIKE mechanism used for every other table is consistent with the design's own stated approach, just an implicit step the design's prose never spelled out.

issues.title: Dimension #2 (columns) as literally specified compares information_schema.columns.ordinal_position directly, which false-fails on every table with a dropped column (REQ-064's ten tenant_id-drop migrations leave permanent ordinal gaps in the template that LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL renumbers away in the clone) -- fixed by comparing each side's own RELATIVE column order (re-ranked 1..N) instead of the raw absolute integer.
issues.description: Reproduced directly against instance_projections and users (both have a dropped tenant_id column at a mid-table position): the template's ordinal_position sequence has a gap (1,3,4,5,...) the clone's does not (1,2,3,4,...), even though every live column's relative order and every other column property is identical. This is a benign difference LIKE was never claimed to preserve (Postgres renumbers to consecutive positions when creating a new table with LIKE, regardless of the source's own dropped-column history) -- not a real divergence in the sense dimension #2 is meant to catch, so re-ranking rather than comparing raw values is the correct fix, not a weakening of the check.

issues.title: Implementation bug (mine, not the design's): dimension #4 (indexes) initially compared the full indexdef STRING including the index's own auto-generated name, contradicting the design's own explicit instruction (§0.1 finding 2) that index comparison must be structural/name-independent -- fixed by stripping the `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX <name>` prefix before comparison, keeping only the ON-clause-forward structural remainder plus a separately-tracked uniqueness flag. Same fix applied preemptively to dimension #11 (pg_statistic_ext) for the identical reason (design §0.2 finding 4), though that dimension is a confirmed zero-vs-zero rule-out today so it was not exercised by real data this session.
issues.description: Reproduced directly: a real, structurally-correct clone with all 105/105 indexes present and structurally identical was reported as 105 mismatches by my first implementation, purely because LIKE ... INCLUDING ALL auto-renames every index (e.g. events_parent_idx -> events_parent_id_idx, exactly as design §0.1 finding 2 documents) and my comparison included that name in the compared string. This was my own coding error against an already-correct design instruction, not a design defect -- recorded as MINOR because it was caught and fixed within this same step before handoff, but noted so REVIEWER can specifically re-check dimension #4 and #11's structural-comparison logic rather than trusting my self-report.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER (not REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER -- this is a design-premise defect, not an implementation-quality question) to: (1) correct the trigger-dormancy claim in the design doc, (2) design the trigger-recreation mechanism this now-live OQ-2 scenario requires (function-body copy + schema-qualifier rewrite + CREATE TRIGGER in the clone, symmetric to the already-proven FK-rewrite technique), (3) spot-check whether any other 'currently dormant' claim in the design has gone stale since 20260830's migrations landed. Once CODE-DESIGNER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR re-gate a corrected design, ELIXIR-DEV (this role, likely the same run continued) adds the trigger-recreation step to clone_tenant_schema!/1 and re-verifies dimension #8 passes non-vacuously on a real clone, then completes the deferred work: a representative timing measurement (today's ~1.0x ratio is not representative of a complete mechanism and must be re-measured once trigger recreation is added, since that is real additional DDL cost this session's timing numbers do not include), and a real run of an existing test file using the fixture's new :clone default. This handoff's own code (test/support/tenant_template.ex, test/support/tenant_fixture.ex) is left in place, uncommitted per this run's 'ORCH commits' instruction -- it is a correct, working implementation of dimensions #1-7 and #9-13, and only dimension #8 plus its still-missing mechanism step block full completion.
